result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both screenshots show only the top of each page, so the sample form, card and status message could not be seen, and items 1 and 4 are scored with low confidence. B wins narrowly: its tier model (raw values → color/type roles → components, with 'never skip a tier') and its rule for adding new pieces ('adapt an existing piece first; if a second screen needs it, it joins the system') give stronger structure and guidance, and it supports theming. A looks warmer and calmer in its light, clinic-like palette and has short, clear numbered rules, but it shows less of how color is organized by job. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Only the top of each page is visible, so I couldn't see either answer's sample form, card or status message, and those scores are estimates. B's warm off-white and deep teal look calmer and more like a clinic, and its numbered 'How we build' rules (tokens only, add a token first, never color alone, one primary action) are short and easy to follow. A has a smart raw-value → role → component token setup and a theme toggle, but it shows in a heavy dark mode by default, which feels less warm and friendly for pet owners.
